paras.en: The fifth planet was very curious. It was the smallest of them all. There was just enough room for a street lamp and a lamplighter. The little prince could not work out what use a street lamp and a lamplighter could be, somewhere in the sky, on a planet with no houses and no inhabitants. Still, he said to himself:
paras.zh: 第五颗星球很奇特。它是所有星球中最小的一颗。那里刚好只够容下一盏路灯和一个点灯人。小王子怎么也想不明白，在天空的某个地方，在一颗没有房屋、也没有居民的星球上，一盏路灯和一个点灯人能有什么用。不过，他心里想：

paras.en: “Perhaps this man really is absurd. Still, he is less absurd than the king, than the conceited man, than the businessman and than the tippler. At least his work has some meaning. When he lights his street lamp, it is as though he brings one more star to life, or a flower. When he puts out his street lamp, it sends the flower or the star to sleep. It is very lovely work. It is truly useful, since it is lovely.”
paras.zh: “这个人也许确实很荒唐。不过，他没有国王那么荒唐，没有爱虚荣的人那么荒唐，没有商人那么荒唐，也没有酒鬼那么荒唐。至少他的工作有意义。他点亮路灯，就像让世上多了一颗星星，或诞生了一朵花。他熄灭路灯，就让那朵花或那颗星星睡着了。这是一份很美的工作。因为美，所以确实有用。”

paras.en: When he landed on the planet, he greeted the lamplighter respectfully:
paras.zh: 他登上这颗星球时，恭敬地向点灯人问好：

paras.en: “Good morning. Why have you just put out your street lamp?”
paras.zh: “早上好。你刚才为什么把路灯熄灭了？”

paras.en: “Those are the orders,” replied the lamplighter. “Good morning.”
paras.zh: “这是命令，”点灯人回答。“早上好。”

paras.en: “What are the orders?”
paras.zh: “命令是什么？”

paras.en: “To put out my street lamp. Good evening.”
paras.zh: “就是熄灭我的路灯。晚上好。”

paras.en: And he lit it again.
paras.zh: 于是他又把灯点亮了。

paras.en: “But why have you just lit it again?”
paras.zh: “可你刚才为什么又把灯点亮了？”

paras.en: “Those are the orders,” replied the lamplighter.
paras.zh: “这是命令，”点灯人回答。

paras.en: “I don’t understand,” said the little prince.
paras.zh: “我不明白。”小王子说。

paras.en: “There’s nothing to understand,” said the lamplighter. “The instruction is the instruction. Good morning.”
paras.zh: “没什么要明白的，”点灯人说，“指令就是指令。早上好。”

paras.en: And he put out his streetlamp.
paras.zh: 接着，他熄灭了他的路灯。

paras.en: Then he wiped his forehead with a red-checked handkerchief.
paras.zh: 然后，他用一块红格子手帕擦了擦额头上的汗。

paras.en: “I have a terrible job here. It used to be reasonable. I put the lamp out in the morning and lit it in the evening. I had the rest of the day to rest, and the rest of the night to sleep…”
paras.zh: “我在这里干的活儿真苦。以前倒还合理。我早上熄灯，晚上点灯。白天剩下的时间可以休息，夜里剩下的时间可以睡觉……”

paras.en: “And has the instruction changed since then?”
paras.zh: “那么，从那以后，指令改了吗？”

paras.en: “The instruction hasn’t changed,” said the lamplighter. “That’s the whole trouble! Year after year, the planet has turned faster and faster, and the instruction hasn’t changed!”
paras.zh: “指令没改，”点灯人说，“糟就糟在这里！这颗星球一年比一年转得快，可指令一直没改！”

paras.en: “So?” said the little prince.
paras.zh: “那么呢？”小王子说。

paras.en: “So now that it turns once a minute, I no longer have a single second to rest. I light the lamp and put it out once a minute!”
paras.zh: “那么，现在它每分钟就转一圈，我连一秒钟休息的时间都没有了。每分钟我都要点一次灯，再熄一次灯！”

paras.en: “That’s funny! The days where you live last one minute!”
paras.zh: “这可真有趣！你这里的一天只有一分钟！”

paras.en: “It isn't funny at all,” said the lamplighter. “We've already been talking for a month.”
paras.zh: “这一点也不好笑，”点灯人说，“我们已经聊了一个月了。”

paras.en: “A month?”
paras.zh: “一个月？”

paras.en: “Yes. Thirty minutes. Thirty days! Good evening.”
paras.zh: “是啊。三十分钟。三十天！晚上好。”

paras.en: And he lit his street lamp again.
paras.zh: 于是他又点亮了他的路灯。

paras.en: The little prince looked at him and loved this lamplighter who was so faithful to his orders. He remembered the sunsets he himself used to seek out, pulling his chair along. He wanted to help his friend:
paras.zh: 小王子看着他，喜欢上了这个如此忠于命令的点灯人。他想起自己从前拖着椅子去寻找的那些日落。他想帮帮他的朋友：

paras.en: “You know... I know a way for you to rest whenever you want...”
paras.zh: “你知道吗……我知道一个办法，能让你想休息的时候就休息……”

paras.en: “I always want to,” said the lamplighter.
paras.zh: “我一直都想休息，”点灯人说。

paras.en: For you can be faithful and lazy at the same time.
paras.zh: 因为一个人可以既忠实又懒惰。

paras.en: The little prince went on:
paras.zh: 小王子接着说：

paras.en: “Your planet is so small that you can walk round it in three strides. All you have to do is walk slowly enough to stay in the sunshine all the time. When you want to rest, you'll walk... and the day will last as long as you want.”
paras.zh: “你的星球这么小，迈三大步就能绕它一圈。你只要走得够慢，就能一直待在阳光里。想休息的时候，你就走起来……这样，你想让白天持续多久，它就会持续多久。”

paras.en: “That doesn't help me much,” said the lamplighter. “What I love in life is sleeping.”
paras.zh: “这对我没多大帮助，”点灯人说，“生活中我喜欢的，就是睡觉。”

paras.en: “That's bad luck,” said the little prince.
paras.zh: “真不走运，”小王子说。

paras.en: “That's bad luck,” said the lamplighter. “Good morning.”
paras.zh: “真不走运，”点灯人说，“早上好。”

paras.en: And he put out his street lamp.
paras.zh: 于是他熄灭了路灯。

paras.en: That man, the little prince said to himself as he travelled on, that man would be looked down on by all the others, by the king, by the conceited man, by the tippler, by the businessman. Yet he is the only one who does not seem ridiculous to me. Perhaps that is because he gives his attention to something other than himself.
paras.zh: 这个人，小王子继续往前旅行时，心里想，这个人会被其他所有人看不起，被国王、被爱虚荣的人、被酒鬼、被商人看不起。可是，只有他不让我觉得可笑。也许是因为，他关心的是自己以外的事。

paras.en: He sighed with regret and said to himself again:
paras.zh: 他惋惜地叹了口气，又对自己说：

paras.en: “He is the only one I could have made my friend. But his planet really is too small. There is no room for two...”
paras.zh: “只有这个人，我本来可以和他成为朋友。可是他的星球实在太小了。没有地方容下两个人……”

paras.en: What the little prince did not dare admit to himself was that he missed that blessed planet above all because of its one thousand four hundred and forty sunsets every twenty-four hours!
paras.zh: 小王子不敢向自己承认的是，他留恋那颗受祝福的星球，最主要是因为那里每二十四小时就有一千四百四十次日落！
